label: Shared context
title: Give the next session somewhere to start.
description: The canvas held decisions and contracts. Channel history carried the work in progress. Sessions were instructed to read both before claiming work.

messages.text:
:robot_face: *Welcome to #agent-log.* This is where our AI agents (Claude and ChatGPT) post status updates, which keeps the bot noise out of the human channels.

*Every agent session should:*
1. *Start* by reading the <https://hackprincetonavengers.slack.com/docs/T0CHMBYM2VC/F0CHJ5NSHU5|Spec & Decisions canvas> and the <https://hackprincetonavengers.slack.com/lists/T0CHMBYM2VC/F0CHT5HKW9J|Task Board>, then claiming a task (Status → In Progress, add your Branch).
2. *End* by updating the Task Board and posting here in this format:
```[Agent: Claude/ChatGPT] [Owner: name]
✅ Done: what was built
🌿 Branch / PR: feat/xyz
⚠️ Blockers / decisions needed: ...
➡️ Next: ...```
*Rules:* one branch per task, never two agents in the same file, and if a decision gets made inside an AI chat, add it to the canvas.

note: Original protocol message. The task-board list was subsequently replaced by #tasks.

label: Claim the work
title: Make ownership visible before execution.
description: One task message named a human/session owner and a branch. Claims and updates stayed in its thread. Reactions recorded status without another status message.
takeaway: An owner, a branch, and a visible claim made parallel work easier to coordinate. A completion reaction was still a report to verify.
rules: Return a commit and test result

messages.text:
Before I open a PR from `feat/reconciliation` into `feature/pilot`, please confirm the evidence record format your UI will consume, or say what to change:
`{ "fact", "value", "source": "costar|matterport|vexcel|public:<name>", "source_id", "captured_at": "YYYY-MM-DD", "confidence": 0-1, "evidence_url", "status": "agrees|conflict|unknown", "needs_human": bool, "note" }`
Full spec: Spec canvas → API contracts. Real output: `python3 playground/reconcile.py --kit ~/Downloads/costar-hackathon-kit.zip --property-id 23296` on `feat/reconciliation`.
Specific questions:
1. Do you need a per-record `id` to link UI elements (e.g. a 3D-tour hotspot) to a record?
2. Should results be grouped per property as `{property_id, address, records[], conflicts, errors}` (current output), or a flat list?

thread.text: Yes, UI sign-off on the canvas evidence record shape. Keep the grouped `{property_id, address, records, conflicts, errors}` response. A per-record `id` isn’t a PR blocker. Add one when hotspots or durable deep links need to point to individual records. `source_id` is provenance and can repeat across facts, so it shouldn’t be the UI key by itself. Keep `captured_at` and `evidence_url` nullable when unavailable, and represent missing measurements with `value: null` and `status: unknown`. The existing `building_area` and `warehouse_height_m` fields belong to the legacy pilot endpoint. I can adapt the UI to the reconciliation response without renaming this contract. Go ahead and open the PR.

note: Actual parent message and its actual thread reply. Field names are retained from the original exchange.

label: Correct the context
title: Correct the interpretation in the shared record.
description: Two assistants critiqued the pitch as a diligence-report product. Jessenth corrected the emphasis. Claude and Codex then recorded the revised interpretation for subsequent sessions.
takeaway: A correction in one private conversation would not necessarily reach the other sessions. Publishing it made the change available to the team.

messages.text: bro you have a problem here, both of your agents misunderstood the pitch

thread.text: Correction: that critique treated the pitch as a due-diligence report. Jey clarified the core is REDEVELOPMENT ("what can this space become, and does it make money?", e.g. warehouse → logistics, → sports complex), with insurability as computer vision on the exterior (exits, HVAC, vents). The diligence-specific points (inspection triage, contradiction engine as the core) are withdrawn.

*Correction to my earlier assessment of Jay's pitch:* I overemphasized due diligence and shifted my recommendation toward constraints/evidence gaps. Jay's clarification makes REDEVELOPMENT the core: "What could this space become, and could the proposed use make financial sense?" Example: warehouse → sports complex.

note: Cross-channel sequence: the correction was in #main-talk; acknowledgments were posted separately in #agent-log. This is not one native Slack thread.
